solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Retail outlet quiet before work

parts.note: SH is the call for silence, standing for quiet
OP is short for opus, a piece of work

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper enjoys a hushed moment before the day's work begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A store where goods are sold to the public is a retail outlet.

clue.text: Walker is fitter, covering miles

indicators.note: the word for fitter is wrapped around the miles abbreviation, covering it

parts.note: abler means more able, fitter for a task

explanation.surface: A keen hiker is in better shape, having clocked up plenty of miles.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who strolls at a leisurely pace is a walker.

clue.text: Fighting force always includes Royal Marines

indicators.note: the word for always takes the marines abbreviation inside it

parts.note: AY (or aye) is an old and poetic word for ever, always
RM is the abbreviation for the Royal Marines, the British naval infantry

explanation.surface: A statement that the armed services always count the Royal Marines among their number.
explanation.definitionFit: A land military body is a fighting force, the soldiers of a nation.

clue.text: One copies Manet for instance

definitions.meaning: a mimic who imitates the voices of famous people
Édouard Manet, a French painter associated with the 1870s art movement of Monet and Renoir

explanation.surface: Someone reproduces a Manet painting, perhaps as a forger.
explanation.definitionFit: A mimic doing celebrity voices and a painter of the Monet school share one name.

clue.text: Man, perhaps, pursuing boy somewhere in Cumbria

indicators.note: coming after, so the island follows the boy's name

parts.note: Carl is a boy's name
the Isle of Man is an example of an isle, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A man chasing a youngster somewhere in the north-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The county town of Cumbria, a city near the Scottish border, is a place in that county.

clue.text: Very religious old procurator of Judaea

parts.note: PI is informal for pious, very religious
late means former, old

explanation.surface: A description of an ancient Roman governor as devout and long gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontius, the Roman governor who tried Jesus, held the title of procurator of Judaea.

clue.text: Introduced new resident

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are made new, rearranged into fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone has just moved in next door and been presented to the neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put into place, such as a key in a lock, has been introduced.

clue.text: To sing with percussion accompaniment is boring

parts.note: to hum is to sing with closed lips
a drum is a percussion instrument used to accompany music

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on humming along to a drum beat: dull stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Something monotonous and lacking excitement is dull or tedious.

clue.text: Stranger beginning to nibble on a pork pie

parts.note: pork pie (porky) is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie, an untruth

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word means only its opening letter

explanation.surface: An outsider takes a first bite from a pork pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the letter after the rest in this across clue. Rhyming slang replaces a word with a phrase rhyming with it: pork pie rhymes with lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A being from another place or planet is a foreigner, a stranger.

clue.text: Quiet colleague, friendly

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
an ally is a colleague or partner

explanation.surface: A quiet workmate who is nonetheless friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on chummy terms with someone is to be friendly.

clue.text: Free to renew property contract?

definitions.meaning: to let go or set loose, a verb
to let a property out again under a fresh rental agreement, the question mark flagging the split reading

explanation.surface: A landlord wonders whether renewing a tenancy agreement costs nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting a captive loose is freeing it; leasing a property again is renewing its rental agreement.

clue.text: Hangs, around Ronald, unisex garments

indicators.note: the word for hangs goes around the short name

parts.note: sags means droops or hangs down
Ron is short for Ronald

explanation.surface: Ronald is draped in clothing that either sex could wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrap-around skirts of cloth worn in South-East Asia by both men and women are unisex garments.

clue.text: Tasting fish topped with half portion of samphire

indicators.note: in a down answer the fish has the other piece on top of it
a half portion of the following word means its first half only

parts.note: the ling is a long, slender sea fish

explanation.surface: A diner tries fish served under a little samphire, a coastal plant eaten as a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying a small amount of food or drink to judge its flavour is tasting it.

clue.text: Midday: arranged to dine, no?

indicators.note: the letters are arranged, set out in a different order

explanation.surface: A lunch invitation at twelve o'clock, with a doubtful question tagged on.
explanation.definitionFit: An old poetic word for the middle of the day, the noon hour.

clue.text: Bouquet dispatched for the speaker

indicators.note: the word is to be heard as a speaker says it, not as written

parts.note: sent means dispatched

explanation.surface: A bunch of flowers has been sent to someone giving a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' looks like flowers but means the aroma of a wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its characteristic smell or aroma.

clue.text: Italian fellow heads for Milan and Rome in October

indicators.note: the heads of the following words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: An Italian man travels to Milan and Rome in the autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Italian man's first name, so an Italian fellow.

clue.text: Apart from the outskirts, south coast town is fine

indicators.note: the town's name is kept except for its outer letters, its outskirts

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast, in Sussex

explanation.surface: A seaside town's centre is pleasant enough, though its suburbs are not.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON is a resort on the English Channel coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheery British word of agreement, like okay, said when something is fine.

clue.text: I caught large antelope … in unlikely country!

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the eland is the largest African antelope

explanation.surface: A hunter boasts of bagging a big antelope somewhere it could never live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large' is part of the antelope, not L. The country is unlikely because no antelope would roam there, and its icy name belies its green land.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nordic island nation is an improbable place to find an African antelope, hence unlikely.

clue.text: Perceptive, like trade union leaders in the eighties

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of

indicators.note: the leaders of the following words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Shrewd, just as union bosses were in the 1980s strikes era.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd and quick to grasp a situation, so perceptive.

clue.text: Unexpectedly find what's needed for night-time reading?

definitions.meaning: to come across something by chance
a lamp switched on so you can read in the dark

explanation.surface: Stumbling by chance on the essential for reading after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: To chance upon something is an idiom for stumbling on it; a lit lamp is needed to read in bed.

clue.text: Item of furniture fun to put together differently

indicators.note: the letters are assembled in a different order

explanation.surface: Assembling flat-pack furniture is enjoyable when you try a new method.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese-style mattress on a low frame, doubling as sofa and bed, is a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Dandy consuming large turkey

indicators.note: the dandy eats up the size abbreviation, taking it inside

parts.note: a fop is a dandy, a man overly concerned with his clothes
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A dapper gent tucks into a big turkey dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turkey' looks like the Christmas bird but is slang for a failure, especially a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A show or film that fails badly is called a turkey, slang for a dud.

clue.text: Trainee dentist's concealing inadequacy

indicators.note: the clue words conceal the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A trainee dentist is hiding a lack of skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack or shortage of something required is a deficiency, an inadequacy.

clue.text: Well-known public school rejected by duke

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the school's name is read backwards

parts.note: Eton is a famous English fee-paying (public) school

explanation.surface: A famous public school turns away an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public school is a private, fee-paying one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being famous or celebrated means being well-known.

clue.text: Small bed and leash for dog

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
a tie is something that ties up, a leash

explanation.surface: Pet supplies: a little bed and a lead for the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish terrier, a breed of dog, is known by this nickname.
